name: Party Crasher
why: Joining a taken space bends the core blocking rule; the owner picks the one big moment and the blocked player feels it.

name: Big Spender
why: A one-time double recruit is a timing choice, but a modest payoff with no one else noticing.

name: Alchemists
why: Paying colored costs with anything opens every color's shop to you at worth 3; strong and cross-color, but shares a name with the gold Alchemists.

name: Extra Hand
why: Nine resources for one extra minion once and 1 follower is a poor trade beside a follower pack; nobody else feels it.

name: Line Cutters
why: Cheap, worth 3, and going first forever removes the fewest-followers catch-up order; must-buy and leader-friendly.

name: Launderers
why: Rearranging everything on recruit lets you jump a contest at worth 3 for 4; strong, plain, little drama.

name: Old Maid
why: Only works as a hot potato for swap and give cards; a real dumping game, but never a card you want to buy.

name: Dabblers
why: 'Wild member' needs a ruling on which counts it joins; quiet value for set and per-color scorers.

name: Cheerleader
why: +1 follower for winning a contest the winner already won; forgettable and rewards the leader.

name: Anarchist
why: A swap anywhere every round is a sting and a lever; 'within 2' needs a quick check each time.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancelling a contest you can't win is a big sting, a strong catch-up tool, and makes every rim tense.

name: Con Men
why: Steal 5 on arrival is a real sting, but a one-shot that builds nothing.

name: Coach
why: A second use of a once-per-game member is a nice combo, only as good as your On Use members.

name: Sore Loser
why: Stealing 3 followers from the big contest winner when you won none is catch-up the table feels.

name: Tiebreaker
why: Winning every tie changes how you read every rim; clear and quiet.

name: Build Up
why: The plain anchor; a fine scaling gain with no story.

name: Echo
why: Copying the previous action makes you watch what the player before you took and scales into later rounds.

name: Reprise
why: Copying your own action again rewards having placed well; mostly solitary.

name: Sample
why: Borrowing a rival's On Recruit makes you read their cult; which effects copy cleanly needs a ruling.

name: Cover
why: Copying an empty space gives reach without blocking anyone; a quiet choice.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Firing every On Recruit again is the burst a green cult builds toward.

name: Busker
why: Steady +2 green income; fine and cheap, but works the same in any cult.

name: Muse
why: +1 green when a rival copies; tiny and nobody notices.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrowing a rival's best ability each round is a sting and a real aim; needs a marker on the chosen card.

name: Understudy
why: Copies whatever the previous turn was; works but feels random and small.

name: Ensemble
why: Worth 3 plus a follower per self-copy; 'your own action' needs a ruling between Echo and Reprise.

name: Impressionist
why: +1 of a color whenever anyone copies; a forgettable trickle.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubling every copy's gain turns Echo and Cover into big turns; pricey but a real engine.

name: Fan Club
why: Copying a space the leader sits on is aimed catch-up at worth 3; reads clean.

name: Roadie
why: Scales with green members, a mono-color snowball; plain income.

name: Stunt Double
why: Doubling the space you just took makes you plan the turn you buy it; clean combo with Initiation or Help Yourself.

name: Tribute Band
why: Doing every action a rival took is a huge round III moment; 14 resources is steep and reach can be hard to read.

name: Doppelganger
why: Doubling your best member is a solid combo, mostly solitary.

name: Impostors
why: Copying a rival's member is fine but overlaps Impersonator and Doppelganger.

name: Agents
why: A clean block on copying; the green player feels it, nothing builds.

name: Bait
why: A trap on your own spaces that stings copiers; makes green think twice.

name: Chronicler
why: The generic per-member-of-my-color scorer every color has; nothing green about it.

name: Allowance
why: The same resource-plus-follower template as Gather and Stash; nothing white about it.

name: Splurge
why: Followers for paying big makes a pricey recruit pay twice; round III's rate isn't printed.

name: Exchange
why: A clean resource-to-followers conversion; useful, quiet.

name: Farewell
why: Casting out a member for its cost in followers is a dramatic choice and combos with Martyrs and Undertaker.

name: Estate Sale
why: The weaker twin of Farewell, paying white instead of followers.

name: Cash In
why: The round III cash-out of a white pile; clean payoff, mostly solitary.

name: Recluse
why: Paying the small cult per rival with more members is real catch-up and a different plan.

name: Landlord
why: Steady +2 white income; works the same in any cult.

name: Heiresses
why: One burst of white per member; rewards the big cult, no one else notices.

name: Brokers
why: Worth 3 plus a follower on each white follower gain; a clear color engine.

name: Exporters
why: +1 white on non-white recruits; a forgettable trickle.

name: Misers
why: End scoring on held white pulls against Cash In, a real choice, but rewards the hoarder.

name: Raiders
why: Stealing 4 followers is a big sting with a little payback, but theft is another color's job.

name: Cashier
why: A cheap cash-out on recruit that lets you pick your moment; overlaps Cash In.

name: Undertaker
why: +2 per cast-out is a clean engine with Farewell and Estate Sale.

name: Money Changers
why: White off everyone's follower buys; the same shape as Tax Collector.

name: Martyrs
why: Paying out its cost when it leaves turns a theft or swap target into a gift and combos with Farewell; everyone thinks before taking it.

name: Old Money
why: Generic per-white-member end scorer.

name: Hoarder
why: Turning everything white once sets up Cash In or the white contest; a timing call.

name: Help Yourself
why: A scaling steal you aim yourself; the color's clear anchor and every rival feels it.

name: Stash
why: The same template as Gather and Allowance; nothing about theft.

name: Lie Low
why: A small steal plus a shield for the round; a real defensive timing choice.

name: Heist
why: Taking 3 followers from the leader is a sting and catch-up.

name: Shake Down
why: The victim chooses pay or lose, a real choice for them; needs a moment to explain.

name: Poach
why: Taking any rival's member for free is the round III punch the color builds to.

name: Cutpurse
why: A cheap steady tax on the richest rival; a check on hoards, little choice.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap one-time steal of 3; fine value, builds nothing.

name: Grifter
why: Eight resources for a member-scaled steal that rewards big cults; rarely worth it.

name: Sticky Fingers
why: +1 on every steal builds a theft engine across the color's spaces.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A steal timed right before contests is a contest snipe everyone has to plan around.

name: Desperado
why: Bigger steals while trailing is clean catch-up.

name: Robin Hood
why: A follower for robbing the leader points theft at the runaway; small.

name: Extortionist
why: A bigger Cutpurse; strong sting, but a copy of a sibling.

name: Bodyguards
why: A full shield against theft is a block, but it protects hoards and builds nothing.

name: Crew
why: A vanilla 2-follower body; nobody reacts.

name: Double Agent
why: Trading this member for a rival's best is a pointed sting and a target choice.

name: Fixer
why: Spending held magenta to take a member ties the pile to theft; a real decision.

name: Kingpin
why: Generic per-member-of-my-color end scorer.

name: Kidnapper
why: Taking the big cult's cheapest member every round is a steady sting aimed at the runaway.

name: Snitch
why: A deterrent tax on thieves; reactive, no choices.

name: Shoplifter
why: A steal on every recruit stacks with Sticky Fingers; steady.

name: Fence
why: +2 magenta when robbed; a consolation that builds nothing.

name: Savings
why: Blue plus a bury before you recruit; a small shop-shaping edge.

name: Out of Style
why: Clearing a whole color from the shop can wreck a rival's plan and pays per member; a real sting.

name: Peek
why: Ordering the top of the pile and recruiting from it; private info that's fiddly at a table.

name: Recruit Twice
why: A second buy when the buy is scarce; strong and plain.

name: Bury
why: Hate-burying the card a rival wants, paid in blue; a clean block.

name: Spree
why: Three buys is the round III burst; strong, solitary.

name: Connoisseurs
why: +1 blue on blue recruits; forgettable.

name: Hawker
why: Rivals pay you a premium or you get it free; an auction-like table moment that takes a read.

name: Bargain Bin
why: +1 blue per bury; tiny, and whether the between-rounds row counts is unclear.

name: Patroness
why: Followers on every bury builds with Out of Style and Window Shopper.

name: Snobs
why: Generic per-member-of-my-color end scorer.

name: Window Shopper
why: Burying two each round and taking their colors; shop control with a payoff.

name: Restockers
why: Wiping the whole shop once is a big timed moment everyone feels.

name: Shopaholics
why: Two buys every turn at worth 3 is a huge engine; rewards whoever is already rich.

name: Window Dressers
why: Worth 3 and a three-card bury on arrival; solid, a smaller Restockers.

name: Plus-Ones
why: Worth 2 and a free extra recruit; good value, quiet.

name: Doormen
why: Swapping a rival's member for a shop member each round is a sting; 'up to 2 less or any more' takes a reread.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue per follower buy; forgettable.

name: Trendsetters
why: Worth 3 and a bury on each recruit; steady shop control.

name: Critic
why: +1 when a rival recruits blue; nobody notices.

name: Scavenger
why: Grabbing what rivals bury punishes their shop play; a real counter.

name: Harvest
why: A plain any-color gain; fine anchor.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Pays on where rivals placed; a quick read of the wheel that changes with the table.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards a new color in your cult this turn; a clear shop-reading choice.

name: Big New Blood
why: A bigger New Blood; strong but a twin of it.

name: Melting Pot
why: Scales with your color spread; a broad-cult payoff.

name: Makeover
why: Rearranging everything at round III can flip a contest; a clean finale.

name: Gardener
hardFail: multi-member card with a singular name
why: Fills missing colors each round; nice for a broad cult and kind to a player behind, but counts as 2 under a singular name.

name: Customs Officer
why: +1 yellow when robbed; tiny, reactive, nobody notices.

name: Go-Between
why: Flex 1 resource per space; handy, quiet.

name: Tourist
why: A follower per color held each round makes a broad pile score; a clear engine.

name: Tinker
why: A small swap each round; fine, forgettable.

name: Harmonist
why: End scoring on full sets; 'full set' needs a definition.

name: Matchmaker
why: Rewards new colors; overlaps New Blood and Guest Book.

name: Dyer
why: Yellow per color held; plain scaling income.

name: Meddler
why: Changing every rival's resource can break contest leads; a sting with a follower each.

name: Drifters
why: Choosing its color turns on per-color scorers and New Blood; a cheap flexible piece.

name: Leveler
why: Converting rivals' biggest piles every round knocks the leader off contests; a strong aimed tool.

name: Big Tent
why: +2 per color with exactly one member drives a spread-out cult; distinct plan.

name: Book Cookers
why: A once-per-game rearrange worth 3; copies Makeover and Launderers.

name: Caravan
why: +1 of each held color every round at worth 3; strong income that rewards the leader.

name: Tastemaker
why: Pays for Meddler and Leveler style changes; niche.

name: Spice Route
why: End scoring on colors with 3 or more; a mild hold-versus-spend pull.

name: Guest Book
why: +2 yellow on a new color; a small cheap trickle.

name: Toast
why: A big scaling gain that tops up rivals; a gift everyone notices.

name: Polish
why: A plain conversion; useful, no story.

name: Party Gifts
why: Followers for gifts that feed rivals' silver contest; a real give-and-take choice.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pick what to give and get silver back; a small table moment.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Silver plus a conversion; a twin of Polish.

name: Largesse
why: Up to 10 followers for handing the silver contest to rivals; a dramatic round III call.

name: Hangers-On
why: More from every gift a rival gives you; works with Toast and Potluck.

name: Godparent
why: Giving a member for followers equal to its cost is a gift with a sting; combos with Old Maid.

name: Gift Wrapper
why: +1 per gift action; a clean small engine.

name: Hostesses
why: Gifts every round for a follower each; steady and the table notices.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver when silver is gifted; forgettable.

name: Toastmaster
why: +1 per Silver space; cheap and plain.

name: Debutantes
why: A one-time silver double that tops rivals up; timing choice.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as any color is strong but costs 11; rarely the pick.

name: Philanthropist
why: A small Largesse on recruit; fine.

name: Polisher
why: A one-time Polish; cheap, copies the space.

name: Collector
why: +1 silver when a rival pays silver; nobody notices.

name: Creditor
why: Taking 2 followers each round and paying silver back is a sting with a gift; very silver.

name: Debt Collectors
why: A one-time silver grab; reads like gold.

name: High Society
why: A follower when rivals use Silver spaces; makes the color's spaces a tax.

name: Sleep In
why: A big gain for going last; a real tradeoff on the snake.

name: Hold Up
why: Skipping the next turn, even your own, is a sting with a risk.

name: Right Away
why: A double turn to grab two spaces; clean timing.

name: Last Call
why: Followers per minion left for going last; strong but takes a read.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row to claim key spaces; a clear timing burst.

name: Overtime
why: +1 minion at round III; fine, plain.

name: Go-Getter
why: A once-per-game extra minion right now; a timing choice.

name: Late Risers
why: An extra first minion while trailing is catch-up that bends turn order.

name: Courier
why: +1 of each other color on double turns; an engine with Right Away and Crunch Time.

name: Clockmakers
why: Opening with two turns in a row each round; solid tempo.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays when rivals take Goes Last; when 'on it' is counted needs a ruling.

name: Night Owls
why: An extra minion each round from II; strong, costly.

name: Early Birds
why: Immunity to skips; a quiet block.

name: Bouncers
why: Skipping two rivals on arrival is a sting the table feels.

name: Pocket Watch
why: +2 purple on any skip; a small engine with Hold Up and Bouncers.

name: Gossip
why: Pocket Watch paying a follower; a sibling copy.

name: Extra Shift
why: Nine resources for one extra minion once; poor value.

name: Timekeeper
why: Generic per-member-of-my-color end scorer.

name: Closer
why: +4 for the round's last minion works with Goes Last; a timing race.

name: Hot Streak
why: Followers per turn in a row before it rewards stacking Crunch Time; the count needs care.

name: Shift Crew
why: Worth 4 for 4, no ability; a must-buy body nobody reacts to.

name: Night Shift

why: Can't be read cold: whose minion, after which skip, placed when; needs memory a table can't keep.

name: Tryout
why: Borrowing a shop member's On Recruit makes you read the row; clean.

name: Gather
why: Resources plus followers on a recruit; the plain anchor.

name: Walk-In
why: A blind free recruit that pays rivals; a gamble, mild.

name: Promote
why: Trading up with a rival's member is the color's sting and a target choice.

name: Demote
why: Trading down for red; a real choice of whom to hit.

name: Initiation
why: A free member up to 8 is the round III payoff; strong, plain.

name: Triplets
why: Three bodies for 3; must-buy value with no ability.

name: Body Snatchers
why: An equal-cost swap every round is a steady sting; same-cost matching takes a check.

name: Volunteer
why: A 1-cost body; nobody notices.

why: Worth 3 plus a free cheapest member; solid value.

name: Proselytizers
why: A follower per recruit makes red's free recruits pay; clear engine.

name: Mob

name: Recruiter
why: +1 red per recruit; a forgettable trickle.

name: Host

name: Patriarch
why: End scoring on member count; generic.

name: Greeters
why: Extra resource on your On Recruits; 'that member's color' is unclear for grey.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Worth 4 for 3 with a sting on swaps; underpriced, must-buy.

name: Panel
why: Worth 3 and a swap on arrival; strong red value.

name: Loyalists
why: Blocks swaps; a defense that protects the leader.

why: Swapping a rival's member into the shop for a pricier one is a strange gift; who benefits takes thought.

name: Clerk
why: +1 red a round; dull.

name: Kickback

name: Golden Years
why: A plain scaling gain.

name: Intro Offer
why: A 4-off discount feels good but is solitary.

name: Collect Debts
why: A small gold steal; borrows theft from another color.

name: Tithe
why: Gold per member; rewards the big cult.

why: Doubling gold is the hoard's finale; great for the leader, dead for the rest.

name: Banker

name: Prospector
why: +1 on gold gains; forgettable.

name: Tax Collector
why: Gold off rivals' follower buys; fine table awareness.

name: Merchant
why: +1 when anyone recruits gold; nobody notices.

name: Penny Pincher

name: Alchemists

why: +1 gold on other-color gains; small, and a single member with a plural name.

name: Speculator
